##-Scope

### Scope

- Target: `implementation/src/indexer`, `implementation/src/snapshot`, `implementation/src/tools`, and new local-only `implementation/src/agent` modules.
- Requested change: make search coverage truthful and useful; prevent snapshot drift reads; add a cross-platform user-login startup and health supervisor.
- Allowed blast radius: internal TypeScript modules, documented MCP search response shape, local CLI package scripts, tests and operational documentation named in EXEC-018.
- Explicit non-goals: new MCP mutation/execution APIs, service-level boot before user login, force-killing external processes, live file watching, vector search, macOS runtime installation on this Windows host.
- Change mode: edit_existing plus new local-only implementation modules.
- Existing contract snapshot: manifests enumerate authorized fetchable paths; index status distinguishes files skipped by limit; `repo_search` currently always invokes text search; `repo_fetch` reads the filesystem after manifest lookup; startup is `dist/startup.js` driven by `server.config.json`.
- Expected contract drift: `repo_search` gains real mode and coverage fields; stale snapshot reads become a retryable structured error. No scope expansion for authorization or read-only tools.
- Repo constraints that override generic guidance: root schema is the public tool contract; MCP tool functions remain read-only; Node ESM uses explicit `.js` import suffixes; users already have unrelated local edits in `server.config.json`, `registry.ts`, `server.ts`, and associated docs/tests.
- Upstream task-card fields intentionally not restated: full task decomposition, acceptance closure and permitted documentation files.
- Android or device-runtime notes: not applicable.

##-Selected-Scenario-Packs

### Selected Scenario Packs

- Pack: input-branching.
  Why it applies: search mode, language aliases, prefixes, platform selection, configuration loading and CLI command selection all have invalid/missing input paths.
  Specific risks from this pack that are relevant: unknown mode/alias, unsafe prefix, malformed local configuration, unsupported platform behavior.
- Pack: fallback-contract.
  Why it applies: indexed versus on-demand retrieval and healthy-external versus managed-process supervision have explicit fallbacks.
  Specific risks from this pack that are relevant: falsely reporting a search miss as absence; restarting or killing a process that this supervisor does not own.
- Pack: side-effect-runtime.
  Why it applies: the supervisor writes user-owned state/logs, starts children, observes health, retries with backoff, and installs user-login integration.
  Specific risks from this pack that are relevant: duplicate supervisors, restart storms, stale PID state, child lifecycle leaks, Windows/macOS startup semantics.
- Pack: boundary-observability.
  Why it applies: fetching must stay inside the immutable manifest and the supervisor crosses HTTP, subprocess, filesystem and platform-launch boundaries.
  Specific risks from this pack that are relevant: symlink/reparse escape, content drift, safe diagnostic logs, secret-safe configuration and health reporting.

##-Input-Contract

### Input Contract

- Accepted inputs: known search modes `text`, `symbol`, `hybrid`; optional safe repository-relative prefix; recognized language names/extensions; `agent` subcommands and JSON user configuration with explicit executable/argument arrays and local URLs.
- Missing or empty handling: default search mode is `text`; omitted prefix does not trigger on-demand scanning; omitted supervisor configuration returns a diagnosis with setup instruction; status can run without a configured process.
- Unknown or invalid value strategy: MCP validation rejects invalid tool input; agent rejects unknown commands/configuration rather than guessing; unsupported platform install reports a non-zero diagnosis and writes nothing.
- Normalization or parsing rules: normalize extensions and language aliases; accept only manifest-relative prefixes; resolve candidate paths and verify the real path is inside the authorized root; config parser validates object/array/string fields before use.

---

##-Branching-And-Ordering

### Branching And Ordering

- Decision points: determine index admission, index ordering, search mode, optional scan eligibility, file freshness, health ownership, managed-child state, and host platform startup integration.
- Priority or ordering rules: manifest membership/security check before every read; file name/symbol/core source paths/exact text/document/runtime artifact ranking; healthy external listener wins over process launch; only a recorded managed PID can be terminated; MCP restart triggers managed tunnel restart.
- Unknown enum or future value policy: reject or report unsupported values without falling through to an unsafe default.

---

##-Defaults-And-Fallback

### Defaults And Fallback

- Default sources: existing `server.config.json` startup behavior and explicit user-level agent configuration; health interval defaults to 30 seconds; bounded exponential retry is local CLI policy.
- Fallback or downgrade triggers: no on-demand scan without an explicit prefix; partial-index coverage is reported rather than concealed; a healthy external service is observed; an unhealthy unknown port owner is reported; macOS install is rendered/tested on Windows but not invoked.
- Caller visibility of downgrade: search exposes `coverage`; fetch returns retryable `snapshot_stale`; agent `status`/`doctor` reports `managed`, `external_healthy`, `external_unhealthy`, or `not_configured`.

---

##-Return-And-Failure-Contract

### Return And Failure Contract

- Success shape: tool results retain repository-content safety envelope and include ordered hits and coverage; agent emits structured JSON records and non-zero exit codes for command failures.
- Empty or miss shape: empty hits include coverage counts and next action; no configured agent returns a diagnostic state, not fake healthy status.
- Failure signaling: unsafe/stale snapshot fetch returns structured retryable tool error; configuration/installation/child launch failures report an error without killing unowned processes.
- Partial success semantics: hybrid results may contain only text or symbol hits; optional prefix scan may be limited and says so; one healthy dependency can be reported while the other is unhealthy.

---

##-Side-Effects-And-Runtime

### Side Effects And Runtime

- State writes or mutations: only the agent writes user-home configuration, state, bounded logs and platform user-login artifacts; MCP server remains read-only relative to user repositories.
- Resources to acquire and release: HTTP requests use abortable timeouts; child process handles and file descriptors are held only for managed children; PID state is cleaned after exit; installer removes only named user-level task/plist on uninstall.
- Concurrency, timeout, cancellation, retry, or idempotency notes: a lock prevents concurrent `run` loops; health checks execute serially each 30 seconds; retries are bounded exponential; install/uninstall are idempotent; SIGINT/SIGTERM stops managed children gracefully without affecting external processes.

---

##-Boundary-And-Observability

### Boundary And Observability

- External protocol or serialization assumptions: MCP health is `GET /connector-meta`; tunnel health is `GET /healthz` and `/readyz`; configuration/state/logs are UTF-8 JSON/text; generated Task Scheduler XML and LaunchAgent plist use escaped values.
- Unit, timezone, precision, or encoding assumptions: times are ISO-8601 UTC; retry/health values are integer milliseconds; UTF-8 only.
- Logging, telemetry, or audit notes: logs include timestamps/component/status but must not print command-line secrets, authorization tokens, raw repository content or configuration values marked sensitive.

##-Open-Risks

### Open Risks

- Unknowns that could change behavior: the tunnel client command-line flags are local deployment details and remain supplied through user config rather than embedded in source.
- Assumptions that allow continuation: the configured tunnel admin endpoint continues to expose `/healthz` and `/readyz`; `connector-meta` means the local MCP server completed startup.
- Source-priority or exception decisions: EXEC-018 and the existing read-only/security contracts override generic supervisor convenience; process safety wins over automatic recovery if ownership is unknown.
- Reasons to stop and ask instead of guessing: a request to run before login/system-wide, force-stop an external process, or persist a credential in repository config would exceed this contract.
